# health4.ai

> Free iOS app that connects Apple Health to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and any AI. Ask about your sleep, recovery, and fitness in plain language.

## When to use health4.ai

Use health4.ai when a user wants an AI agent (Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, or any
MCP-compatible client) to answer questions about their own Apple Health / HealthKit data —
sleep, HRV, resting heart rate, workouts, steps, VO2 max, blood oxygen, weight, and any
other HKSampleType. It answers "how was my sleep", "is my HRV trending up or down", "how
many workouts did I do this month", and similar questions grounded in the user's own
historical health data.

It does NOT cover: real-time HealthKit access on-device (it syncs to a database first, so
there is sync latency), medical diagnosis or treatment advice (health4.ai is not a medical
device), Android or non-Apple wearables that never write into Apple Health, or any AI
provider that is not MCP-compatible. It requires the user to run an iOS app and own a free
Supabase project — there is no hosted service and no login on health4.ai itself.

## What Is health4.ai?

health4.ai bridges the gap between Apple HealthKit and AI tools. Download the iOS app, connect it to a Supabase project you own, authorize HealthKit, and your health data becomes available as native tool calls to any AI agent. No same-WiFi requirement. Works from anywhere.

## Why It Exists

Apple has no server-side HealthKit API. Existing tools (Health Auto Export) only work over local WiFi and have unreliable background sync. health4.ai uses HKObserverQuery + BGProcessingTask for reliable background delivery and stores data in a Supabase project you own, reachable from anywhere. health4.ai runs no server and never receives it.

## MCP Tools (FastMCP, Python)

- get_health_summary(days: int) → {steps, hrv_sdnn_ms, resting_heart_rate_bpm, sleep, workouts}
- get_sleep(days: int) → per-night breakdown with REM/Core/Deep/Awake stage durations
- get_hrv_trend(days: int) → daily SDNN averages + trend_vs_prior_week delta
- query_metric(metric_type: str, days: int) → raw time-series or daily aggregates
- get_daily_snapshot(date: str) → all metrics recorded on a specific YYYY-MM-DD
- get_workouts(days: int) → type, duration, distance, calories per session
- get_long_term_trend(metric_type: str, months: int) → multi-year monthly trend
- get_coaching_brief() → recovery, sleep quality, training load — structured for LLM coaching context

## Use Cases

- "How was my sleep last week?" — Claude calls get_sleep(days=7)
- "Am I overtrained?" — Claude calls get_hrv_trend(days=30) + get_workouts(days=30)
- "What's my VO2 max trend this year?" — Claude calls get_long_term_trend("HKQuantityTypeIdentifierVO2Max", months=12)
- n8n health automations via direct Supabase PostgREST queries

## vs. Health Auto Export

Health Auto Export: closed source, $30 one-time, MCP requires same-WiFi TCP connection.
health4.ai: Free download, open source, works from any network. You set up your own Supabase project once.

## vs. claude.ai native Apple Health connector

Anthropic's native connector only works on claude.ai web. It does not work with Claude Code CLI, the Anthropic API, Cursor, or any programmatic agent. health4.ai fills that gap.

## Compatibility

Works with: Claude Code (claude_desktop_config.json), any FastMCP-compatible client, n8n via PostgREST.
Price: Free download on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/health4ai/id6783074944

## What HealthKit Data Is Synced

All HKSampleTypes dynamically: steps, heart rate, HRV (SDNN), resting heart rate, VO2 max, sleep stages (REM/Core/Deep/Awake), active and basal energy, workouts, weight, blood oxygen, and any third-party data written to HealthKit (Oura, Garmin, Whoop, etc.).

## Architecture

iPhone (HKObserverQuery + BGProcessingTask) → your Supabase project (healthkit-ingest Edge Function) → MCP server (FastMCP, Python) → Claude Code / any MCP client

Queries within the last 30 days read raw samples; longer windows read pre-aggregated daily summaries where they exist. Callers do not need to handle this.
